newsitem.title: GERMANY: W.German June CPI seen up 0.2 pct m/m, 1.6 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: W.German June CPI seen up 0.2 pct m/m, 1.6 pct y/y.

text.p: German consumer inflation is expected to have grown slightly on a year-on-year basis in June but should slow in the coming months and will remain below two percent this year, economists said on Monday.

The West German cost of living data is expected to have increased 1.6 percent in June compared with the year-earlier month after having risen 1.5 percent in May, according to an average of forecasts by economists polled by Reuters.
But compared with May 1997, prices in June are forecast to have risen just 0.2 percent after a sharp 0.4 percent increase in May, economists polled by Reuters said.
Data from the four states Hesse, North Rhine-Westphalia, Baden-Wuerttemberg and Bavaria are used to calculate preliminary consumer inflation for west Germany, due to be published on Wednesday.
The predictions were initially confirmed by data from Bavaria which said its consumer prices rose 0.2 percent month-on-month and 1.6 percent year-on-year.
The three other states expect to release their data on Wednesday although North Rhine-Westphalia said there was a chance its inflation may come out on Tuesday.

Economists said consumer prices in May had been driven up by steep increases in the price of package holidays which would keep the annual rate of inflation up in June, whereas the month-on-month increase in June was likely to ease.
But they saw little danger of inflation picking up in the near term.

"Inflation won't rise above two percent this year, I see it at 1.4 to 1.5 percent by end-year due to weak consumer demand, low wage deals and low unit labour costs," said Stefan Bergheim, German economist at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson Research in Frankfurt.
Economists said their forecasts for pan-German inflation were similar to the west German predictions.
In May, the pan-German consumer price index rose 0.4 percent month-on-month and 1.6 percent year-on-year.
